items.title: Beijing Protests After New Zealand Minister Insults Chinese-Born Lawmaker
items.summary: The foreign minister, Winston Peters, who leads a populist party, has refused to back down after telling the member of Parliament to “go back to your own country.”

items.title: Race to rescue remaining climbers after deadly avalanche in Pakistan
items.summary: Poor weather has been hampering the search for seven still missing after Thursday's avalanche on Broad Peak.

items.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv kill at least nine, Ukraine officials say
items.summary: The attack comes as Moscow escalates deadly ballistic missile attacks on the Ukrainian capital.

items.title: Russian Missiles Kill 9 in Kyiv, Hours After Trump Backs Off Air Defense Pledge
items.summary: It was the second deadly barrage to hit the Ukrainian capital in two days, as Moscow escalates its attacks in an apparent effort to exploit Ukraine’s dwindling supply of interceptors.

items.title: Search Continues for 6 Climbers After Pakistan Avalanche
items.summary: Four bodies, including that of an American climber, have been recovered since the avalanche struck on Thursday. The fate of renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja was still unclear.

items.title: Turn failing water firms into not-for-profit cooperatives, MPs and mayors tell PM
items.summary: Labour politicians say mutualised model puts public in control without adding debt to government’s balance sheet MPs and mayors close to Andy Burnham have told the prime minister there is a “third way” to gain more control of failing companies, as the row over whether or not to nationalise Thames Water rumbles on. Burnham is said to be concerned about the increase in government debt that Treasury projections show could be a result of nationalising water companies. Continue reading...

items.title: Trump Backs Away From Deal to Let Ukraine Build Patriot Missiles
items.summary: The president of Ukraine had warned that the country was running out of Patriot interceptors, the most reliable weapon it has to shoot down Russian ballistic missiles.

items.title: Fifa scraps controversial World Cup investment plan
items.summary: Football's world governing body Fifa abandons plans to sell off stakes in its major competitions after widespread opposition to president Gianni Infantino's proposal.

items.title: Israeli West Bank settler tells BBC attacks on Palestinians are justified as revenge
items.summary: Settler violence against Palestinians is on the rise in the West Bank, as settlements and outposts expand.

items.title: ‘Proteinmaxxing’ could lead to higher prices for infant formula, say experts
items.summary: Whey protein, a key infant formula ingredient, is in growing demand, partly linked to rising use of weight-loss drugs The rise of “proteinmaxxing” – a trend in which consumers try to eat as much protein as possible – could lead to higher prices for infant formula, experts warn. Whey protein, a key ingredient in infant formula, has surged in popularity over the past year as health professionals emphasise the benefits of protein. Continue reading...

items.title: Japan’s Rescuers Battle Cruel Heat After Major Earthquake
items.summary: Kumamoto faces a “double disaster,” as rescuers work in 100 degree heat, and shelters with limited air-conditioning put displaced people at risk for heatstroke.

items.title: How 50,000 People Surged Into a Spanish Exclave in Africa
items.summary: On Thursday, tens of thousands of Moroccans broke into Ceuta, a Spanish territory that neighbors Morocco. By Friday evening, most of them had left, hungry and disappointed.

items.title: Extreme Heat Has Transformed What Summer Means Across Generations in Europe
items.summary: Rising temperatures and more frequent heat waves have changed the feel of the season for today’s children, compared with their parents and grandparents.

items.title: ‘Who could have done this?’ Mystery over Briton found dead in a suitcase in Athens
items.summary: Greek police throw entire homicide division at trying to explain fate of 38-year-old Elisabeth-Jane Ross Two worlds separated by sheets of corrugated iron: one, a tree-lined road, bordered by a park and the home of Greece’s oldest sports club; the other a wasteland of derelict buildings and graffiti-covered walls in what was once a car park. It is here, on the wrong side of the divide, in Kypseli, a neighbourhood in central Athens, that the body of Elisabeth-Jane Ross was…

items.title: Singapore bans Massive Attack for showing Palestinian flag, breaching ban on foreign emblems
items.summary: Two members given ‘stern warnings’ after concert and barred from returning, with band also excluded from performing in Singapore again, say authorities British trip-hop band Massive Attack has been barred from performing in Singapore after an investigation found two members unfurled a Palestinian flag during a concert, police said. Singapore, known for its tough laws on public speech and assembly, bans the open display of all foreign flags, national emblems or banners without a permit. Continue reading...

items.title: Peru's ex-president leaves jail after 15-year jail term for corruption overturned
items.summary: Ollanta Humala had been convicted of money laundering offences alongside his wife in 2025.

items.title: Charges Dropped Against Ex-Olympian David Hearn Accused of Damaging Reflecting Pool
items.summary: A former Olympian will not face trial after federal prosecutors acknowledged that the Trump administration’s claims of vandalism were false.

items.title: Officer Charged With Violating Privacy for Recording Colleagues’ Racism
items.summary: The charges stem from recordings that Daniel Flores made over the course of 2024, when he was working in a Los Angeles police unit that recruited new officers.

items.title: George Santos Fined Over Bets on State of the Union on Kalshi Prediction Market
items.summary: A federal regulator fined the former lawmaker $35,000 over allegations of insider trading by placing bets on Kalshi about whether he would attend the State of the Union address in February.

items.title: Missing Australian Hiker Found Dead on Wyoming Trail
items.summary: The man had been traveling the Continental Divide Trail, which goes through five states and is described by a hiking group as one of the “most challenging landscapes in North America.”
